title: Nonlinear Fluctuating Hydrodynamics from Interacting Noisy Quantum Matter
authors: Alexios Christopoulos, João Costa, Stefano Scopa, Jacopo De Nardis, Zala Lenarčič, Denis Bernard, Tony Jin
abstract: A universal characterization of non-equilibrium steady states in interacting quantum many-body systems remains one of the central challenges of statistical physics. Here, we address this problem for a paradigmatic model of diffusive interacting quantum matter---the boundary-driven XXZ spin chain with bulk dephasing---and derive, directly from its microscopic Lindblad dynamics, an emergent classical Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (MFT) governing its large-scale fluctuations. Crucially, the resulting hydrodynamics carries a density-dependent diffusivity and mobility as the fingerprint of interactions. This effective description enables the exact computation of the stationary density profile, long-range correlations, and the full counting statistics of the current, in excellent agreement with tensor-network simulations. Our work demonstrates that noisy quantum many-body systems can realize the universality class of genuinely interacting diffusive matter, beyond the constant-diffusivity class of the symmetric simple exclusion process, and establishes MFT as a powerful universal framework for interacting diffusive quantum systems.
summary: This work tackles the difficult problem of characterizing non-equilibrium steady states in quantum matter by deriving an emergent Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (MFT). Using a boundary-driven XXZ spin chain model, the authors show that the system's large-scale dynamics are governed by nonlinear diffusion equations featuring density-dependent transport coefficients. This establishes MFT as a powerful, universal framework for interacting quantum diffusive systems.
main_problem: The central challenge is deriving a universal hydrodynamic description for non-equilibrium steady states (NESS) in interacting quantum many-body systems.
main_result: The authors derive an emergent classical Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (MFT) for the system, showing that the hydrodynamics features density-dependent diffusivity and mobility.
method: The derivation proceeds by taking a continuum limit of the microscopic Lindblad dynamics, leading to nonlinear diffusion equations for the density field.
model_or_system: The system is a boundary-driven XXZ spin chain with bulk dephasing, whose dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation. The effective low-energy description resembles an Interacting Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process (ISEP).
key_observables: Stationary density profile, long-range correlations, and the full counting statistics of the current.
important_parameters: Density-dependent diffusivity $D( ar{n})$ and mobility $\sigma( ar{n})$, and the scaling limit $	au = s/N^2$.
main_assumptions: The theory relies on a Renormalization Group (RG) argument suggesting a diffusive strong-coupling fixed point, and the slow-mode manifold approximation.
figures_summary: Figures compare tensor-network results for the microscopic model and the ISEP description, showing local diffusivity vs. magnetization and correlation functions.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the microscopic dynamics via Lindblad equations, then uses RG arguments to derive the effective MFT equations, and finally applies this framework to compute observables like correlation functions and full counting statistics.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, microscopic derivation of nonlinear, interacting hydrodynamics, extending the applicability of MFT beyond simple constant-diffusivity models.
